assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is SFT and PEFT (LoRA/QLoRA/DoRA) for fine-tuning pre-trained transformer LLMs
base model is a pre-trained transformer; SFT precedes RLHF/DPO alignment
compute budget is GPU-constrained (single to multi-GPU, not TPU pod scale)
evaluation is task-metric plus general-benchmark centric with contamination controls
exclusions: RLHF and DPO alignment (downstream of SFT)
pre-training and continued pre-training on raw text
inference serving optimization beyond adapter merge
neural architecture search or model distillation
prompt engineering and in-context learning (referenced only for comparison)

competency_questions.question: What criteria determine whether a base model's license permits the target deployment and redistribution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSE_TOS and BASE_MODEL_SEL define classification and audit steps

competency_questions.question: When is fine-tuning a specialist LLM preferable to prompting a frontier generalist model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPECIALIST_VS_GENERALIST defines decision criteria including orchestration cost

competency_questions.question: What standards must instruction-response pairs meet before entering the SFT training pipeline?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATA_FORMAT_QUALITY and DATA_CURATION define quality rubric and filtering

competency_questions.question: How should chat templates be configured to prevent prompt token inclusion in the loss computation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHAT_TEMPLATE node specifies loss masking requirements

competency_questions.question: How are SFT learning rate, epoch count, and batch size selected to prevent divergence and over-training?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYPERPARAM_TUNING node defines selection criteria and pilot run protocol

competency_questions.question: How does SFT training interact with catastrophic forgetting and what mitigation strategy is applied?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAT_FORGETTING node defines detection and mitigation; edges link to SFT_LOOP

competency_questions.question: How are LoRA rank and alpha selected and what target modules should be included for a generative task?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RANK_ALPHA and TARGET_MODULES define selection rationale

competency_questions.question: When should QLoRA be used vs fp16 LoRA and what configuration prevents quantization quality loss?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QLORA_SETUP node and CA_02 define decision criteria and config

competency_questions.question: What compute and memory planning is required to ensure training completes within GPU budget?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPUTE_BUDGET and GRAD_CHECKPOINT_MEM define planning and optimization steps

competency_questions.question: How are training hyperparameters validated to ensure convergence without overfitting the SFT dataset?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYPERPARAM_TUNING + CHECKPOINT_MGT define pilot protocol and early stopping

competency_questions.question: What evaluation suite confirms SFT model quality across task performance and general capability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_HARNESS defines benchmark selection and acceptance thresholds

competency_questions.question: How is benchmark contamination detected and how does Goodhart's law risk affect SFT evaluation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART_BENCH node and CA_05 define contamination detection and mitigation

competency_questions.question: What safety evaluation must be run on the fine-tuned model before production deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAFETY_ALIGNMENT node defines red-team protocol and acceptance gates

competency_questions.question: When should adapters be merged into the base model vs kept separate for multi-adapter serving?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADAPTER_MERGE + CA_09 define the merge vs serve decision criteria

glossary.definition: supervised fine-tuning; training a pre-trained LLM on labeled instruction-response pairs with cross-entropy loss on completion tokens
low-rank adaptation; adds trainable low-rank matrices A,B to frozen base model weight matrices; only A,B are updated during training
quantized LoRA; base model quantized to 4-bit NF4 with double quantization; LoRA adapters trained in fp16/bf16 with paged optimizers
weight-decomposed low-rank adaptation; decomposes weight into magnitude and direction; applies LoRA to directional component with separate magnitude scaling
degradation of pre-trained model's general capabilities when fine-tuned on narrow task data due to gradient overwriting
standardized formatting schema for multi-turn conversations specifying system/user/assistant role tags and special tokens for a given model family
mathematical integration of LoRA adapter weights (W' = W + alpha/r * B*A) into base model weight matrices producing a single merged checkpoint
setting gradient contributions of prompt tokens to zero (-100 label) so the model only learns to predict completion tokens during SFT
integer r controlling the inner dimension of LoRA matrices A (d x r) and B (r x d), determining adapter parameter count as 2*d*r per layer
when a metric becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; in SFT context: optimizing benchmark scores inflates scores without improving true task capability

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for SFT and PEFT work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Tunstall/Werra/Wolf NLP with Transformers, Hu et al. 2021 LoRA, Dettmers et al. 2023 QLoRA, Goodfellow et al. Deep Learning
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Tunstall et al. NLP with Transformers 2022; Hu et al. LoRA arXiv:2106.09685; Dettmers et al. QLoRA arXiv:2305.14314; Liu et al. DoRA arXiv:2402.09353

nodes.definition: Select a pre-trained base model balancing capability, license, compute footprint, and ToS constraints for the fine-tuning task.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new model release or license/ToS change

pros.claim: Locks downstream adapter dims and tokenizer; early decision avoids costly restarts
pros.example: switching from LLaMA-2 to Mistral mid-project forces full data reformat

cons.claim: Base-model license/ToS incompatibility discovered post-training wastes GPU budget
cons.example: LLaMA-2 commercial use clause blocks customer deployment

failure_modes: selecting model whose ToS blocks target use
underestimating quantization quality degradation
acceptance_tests: license confirmed for production use-case
model card benchmark covers target task domain
revisit_triggers: ToS revision or model deprecation
task domain shifts substantially

nodes.definition: Collect, clean, deduplicate, and quality-filter instruction/completion pairs for the SFT regime.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new data source onboarded or quality metrics degrade

pros.claim: High-quality data is the strongest lever for SFT task performance
pros.example: filtering ShareGPT to 52K high-quality samples (Alpaca-style) outperforms 500K noisy pairs

cons.claim: Over-filtering reduces coverage; under-filtering injects noise and misalignment
cons.example: removing all examples under 50 tokens cuts math chain-of-thought data

failure_modes: contaminating eval set with training examples
mixing incompatible instruction formats
acceptance_tests: no eval-set overlap confirmed by n-gram deduplication
data card documents sources and filter thresholds
revisit_triggers: source domain drifts
annotation guidelines updated

nodes.definition: Apply the model-family chat template (system/user/assistant roles, special tokens) and configure the tokenizer for SFT data formatting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: base model or serving framework changes template spec

pros.claim: Correct template prevents EOS/BOS token misalignment that silently degrades generation
pros.example: missing [/INST] in LLaMA-2 chat template causes runaway generation at inference

cons.claim: Template mismatch between training and inference silently degrades output quality
cons.example: training with alpaca template but serving with chatml breaks assistant persona

failure_modes: forgetting to mask prompt tokens in loss (model learns to predict prompts)
EOS token missing causes infinite generation
acceptance_tests: generation terminates correctly on held-out prompts
loss mask confirmed excludes prompt token positions
revisit_triggers: base model replaced (new tokenizer/special tokens)
template spec updated by model provider

nodes.definition: Execute the supervised fine-tuning training loop: forward pass on instruction-completion pairs, compute cross-entropy loss on completion tokens, gradient update.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training loss plateaus or spikes; new data distribution

pros.claim: Direct gradient signal on task outputs produces strong in-domain performance
pros.example: SFT on 1K medical Q&A examples improves F1 by 30pp over prompting

cons.claim: Full fine-tuning requires large GPU memory and risks catastrophic forgetting of general capabilities
cons.example: 7B model full FT needs 4x A100 80GB; fine-tuned on code, loses instruction-following

failure_modes: learning rate too high destroys pretrained weights
epoch over-run causes format memorization not generalization
acceptance_tests: validation loss lower than base model
generation format matches template on held-out prompts
revisit_triggers: task distribution changes requiring retraining
compute budget revised

nodes.definition: Configure LoRA adapter: select target modules, set rank r and scaling alpha, initialize adapter weights, and freeze base model parameters.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new PEFT paper updates rank selection guidance or new model arch

pros.claim: LoRA reduces trainable parameters 100-1000x vs full FT, enabling single-GPU fine-tuning of large models
pros.example: r=16 LoRA on LLaMA-2-7B trains on single A100 40GB vs 4x A100 for full FT

cons.claim: Too-low rank underfits task; too-high rank wastes parameters and memory without matching full FT
cons.example: r=2 on code generation misses complex pattern capture; r=256 gives no benefit over r=64

failure_modes: targeting only attention projections misses MLP contributions for generative tasks
alpha/r ratio mismatch causes training instability
acceptance_tests: adapter adds minimal inference latency overhead confirmed
validation metric with LoRA within 2pp of full FT baseline
revisit_triggers: model architecture updated (new attention mechanism)
task complexity assessment changes rank recommendation

nodes.definition: Configure QLoRA: quantize base model to 4-bit NF4/INT8 with double quantization, attach LoRA adapters, and enable paged optimizers for memory-efficient training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bitsandbytes or transformers library update; new quantization scheme

pros.claim: QLoRA enables 65B model fine-tuning on single 48GB GPU with near-full-FT quality
pros.example: Dettmers et al. 2023: QLoRA matches 16-bit LoRA on MMLU within 1pp

cons.claim: Quantization introduces numerical noise; NF4 quantization error accumulates across layers
cons.example: aggressive 4-bit on small 1.3B models can degrade downstream task performance noticeably

failure_modes: forgetting to set compute_dtype to bf16/fp16 (runs in 4-bit forward, 4-bit backward)
paged optimizer not enabled causing OOM on long sequences
acceptance_tests: training run completes without OOM on target GPU
gradient norms remain stable across first 100 steps
revisit_triggers: bitsandbytes library update changes quantization behavior
new GPU architecture changes optimal config

nodes.definition: Apply DoRA (Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation) which decomposes weights into magnitude and direction components and fine-tunes both with LoRA on the direction.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: PEFT library DoRA API changes or new decomposition paper

pros.claim: DoRA achieves LoRA-quality at lower rank by separately controlling magnitude and directional updates
pros.example: Liu et al. 2024: DoRA r=8 matches LoRA r=16 on commonsense benchmarks

cons.claim: Adds magnitude parameter overhead; implementation in PEFT library still maturing
cons.example: DoRA training slightly slower than LoRA due to norm computation per step

failure_modes: confusing DoRA magnitude with weight scaling hyperparameter alpha
not available for all model architectures in PEFT
acceptance_tests: DoRA magnitude vectors initialized correctly (unit norms)
validation loss comparable to higher-rank LoRA baseline
revisit_triggers: PEFT library DoRA support matures or breaks
new decomposition variant supersedes DoRA

nodes.definition: Select and tune SFT hyperparameters: learning rate, warmup, batch size, gradient accumulation steps, number of epochs, weight decay, and max sequence length.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new scaling law paper updates LR recommendations; architecture change

pros.claim: Learning rate is the single most impactful hyperparameter; correct range prevents divergence or stagnation
pros.example: lr=2e-4 with cosine schedule is robust default for LoRA SFT on 7B models

cons.claim: Exhaustive grid search is compute-prohibitive; heuristic defaults transfer poorly across architectures
cons.example: lr tuned for LLaMA-2 diverges on Falcon architecture

failure_modes: setting lr too high for large rank LoRA causing loss spikes
not accounting for effective batch size in warmup calculation
acceptance_tests: training loss curve smooth (no spikes) with cosine LR schedule
final checkpoint not worse than epoch-1 checkpoint on validation
revisit_triggers: model architecture changes altering learning dynamics
new optimizer (e.g., Adan) adopted

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate catastrophic forgetting of general capabilities during SFT using regularization, replay, or constrained gradient methods.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: general benchmark scores degrade post-SFT; new mitigation technique

pros.claim: Mixing a small fraction of general instruction data preserves capability while achieving task gains
pros.example: 5% replay of Alpaca data prevents MMLU degradation during code SFT

cons.claim: Anti-forgetting techniques add complexity and may reduce peak task performance
cons.example: EWC regularization lowers task-specific F1 by 3pp while preserving general Q&A

failure_modes: not evaluating general benchmarks post-SFT, missing silent degradation
replay data leaking task-specific labels
acceptance_tests: MMLU/HellaSwag scores within 2pp of base model post-SFT
task metric improved over base model baseline
revisit_triggers: task scope expands requiring different general capability preservation
new catastrophic forgetting mitigation method published

nodes.definition: Merge trained LoRA/DoRA adapter weights into the base model for single-artifact deployment, or keep separate for hot-swapping multiple adapters.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deployment architecture change or new merging algorithm adopted

pros.claim: Merged model has zero adapter overhead at inference; identical throughput to base model
pros.example: merged 7B model serves at same latency as base on vLLM

cons.claim: Merging loses adapter modularity; separate adapters enable per-request specialization but add latency
cons.example: multi-tenant serving with 4 adapters adds 15ms per-request vs merged

failure_modes: merging quantized adapters into fp16 base causes precision mismatch artifacts
not validating merged model against adapter model before deployment
acceptance_tests: merged model output matches unmerged adapter+base within fp32 tolerance on 100 test prompts
no performance regression vs unmerged on task benchmark
revisit_triggers: deployment architecture changes to multi-adapter serving
new merge algorithm (TIES, DARE) adopted

nodes.definition: Design and run evaluation harness: task-specific metrics, general capability benchmarks, contamination checks, and human evaluation for SFT model quality assessment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new contamination discovered; task definition changes; Goodhart drift detected

pros.claim: Multi-benchmark evaluation catches capability regression invisible from task-specific metrics alone
pros.example: MMLU reveals forgetting while task F1 shows improvement, preventing premature deployment

cons.claim: Benchmark contamination inflates scores and gives false confidence in model quality
cons.example: training on WizardLM data contaminated with TruthfulQA inflates TruthfulQA scores by 8pp

failure_modes: Goodhart's law: optimizing benchmark metric misaligns with real task quality
using eval set examples for few-shot prompting during eval
acceptance_tests: eval set confirmed not in training data by exact-match deduplication
human eval agreement with automated metric >0.7 Spearman correlation
revisit_triggers: new benchmark contamination discovered
task definition revised requiring new eval protocol

nodes.definition: Select LoRA rank r and scaling factor alpha to control adapter capacity and learning rate effective scale, balancing underfitting vs parameter bloat.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task complexity changes or new rank efficiency analysis published

pros.claim: Rank 8-64 covers most tasks; alpha=2*r is stable default reducing one tuning dimension
pros.example: r=16,alpha=32 robust starting point for instruction tuning on 7B models

cons.claim: High rank increases memory linearly; low rank creates bottleneck for high-complexity tasks
cons.example: r=4 on code-generation task caps model at GPT-3.5 level ceiling

failure_modes: setting alpha != 2r without understanding effective LR scaling
rank too low for multi-task fine-tuning
acceptance_tests: rank ablation shows diminishing returns above chosen rank
alpha/r ratio validated on validation task metric
revisit_triggers: task complexity grows requiring rank increase
new PEFT insight revises rank selection guidelines

nodes.definition: Decide which model layers and projection matrices (Q,K,V,O,up/down/gate projections) to apply LoRA adapters, trading coverage for memory.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new model architecture adopted or task type changes

pros.claim: Including MLP projections alongside attention significantly improves generative tasks
pros.example: code generation: adding gate/up/down projections lifts HumanEval by 5-8pp over q/v only

cons.claim: Adding all linear layers increases trainable parameters and memory; often marginal gain beyond q/k/v/o+MLP
cons.example: embedding LoRA rarely improves task performance but triples adapter size

failure_modes: targeting only q,v but not k and o for tasks requiring cross-attention alignment
module names differ across model families (e.g., c_attn in GPT-2 vs q_proj in LLaMA)
acceptance_tests: all specified target modules exist in model architecture (verified programmatically)
parameter count within VRAM budget
revisit_triggers: model architecture changes (new model family)
task type changes altering which modules matter

nodes.definition: Manage Goodhart's law risk and benchmark contamination: prevent optimizing proxy metrics that diverge from true capability, and detect training-eval overlap.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new contamination methodology published; training data source changes

pros.claim: Early contamination detection prevents deployment of models with inflated benchmark scores
pros.example: MinHash deduplication between training data and MMLU catches 2-4% contamination in web-scraped data

cons.claim: Contamination detection is compute-intensive; perfect isolation impossible for internet-pretrained models
cons.example: n-gram overlap detection misses paraphrase contamination

failure_modes: not running deduplication between SFT data and benchmark test sets
treating benchmark improvement as evidence of real capability gain
acceptance_tests: MinHash or exact-match dedup run between train and eval datasets
benchmark score changes correlated with human eval score changes
revisit_triggers: new benchmark added to eval suite
training data source changes

nodes.definition: Estimate and plan GPU compute budget for SFT: model size, batch size, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and total training tokens to FLOPs mapping.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hardware platform changes or model/dataset scale changes

pros.claim: Accurate FLOP/memory planning prevents mid-training OOM and enables cost-efficient spot instance use
pros.example: Chinchilla scaling laws guide optimal token/parameter ratio for budget

cons.claim: Compute estimates are approximate; actual training can be 1.5-2x estimated due to overhead
cons.example: gradient checkpointing slows training 30-40% vs estimated throughput

failure_modes: underestimating activation memory causing OOM at gradient accumulation step
not accounting for optimizer state in fp32 alongside fp16 model
acceptance_tests: memory profiler confirms peak memory within 90% GPU capacity
cost estimate within 20% of actual spend on 100-step pilot run
revisit_triggers: model size or dataset changes materially
hardware platform changes

nodes.definition: Audit and enforce base model license terms and ToS constraints: permissible use cases, redistribution rights, derivative model sharing, and commercial deployment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: provider updates license; deployment jurisdiction changes

pros.claim: Early license audit prevents costly post-training legal blocks on deployment
pros.example: LLaMA-2 70B commercial use requires explicit Meta approval above 700M MAU threshold

cons.claim: Restrictive licenses block open sharing of fine-tuned models limiting community contribution
cons.example: Mistral Apache-2.0 allows redistribution; LLaMA-2 custom license prohibits training competing LLMs

failure_modes: treating fine-tuned weight merge as derivative work without checking license
ToS change post-training invalidating deployment rights
acceptance_tests: legal sign-off documented for target deployment use case
ToS version recorded in model card
revisit_triggers: model provider updates license terms
new deployment jurisdiction with different requirements

nodes.definition: Evaluate when a fine-tuned specialist LLM beats prompting a generalist model on the narrow task, accounting for orchestration latency/cost compounding.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: frontier model capability jump; task scope change; new cost benchmarks

pros.claim: Fine-tuned specialist consistently beats prompting on narrow structured tasks at lower per-call cost
pros.example: SQL generation: fine-tuned 7B beats GPT-4 few-shot on spider benchmark at 1/50 cost

cons.claim: Specialist beats generalist only on narrow tasks; orchestration overhead compounds in multi-step pipelines
cons.example: 3-specialist pipeline with 150ms each latency vs 1 GPT-4 call at 400ms loses on latency budget

failure_modes: assuming specialist always wins without benchmarking against few-shot prompting of frontier model
ignoring orchestration latency when comparing multi-specialist vs single-generalist cost
acceptance_tests: benchmarked specialist outperforms best few-shot prompting baseline by statistically significant margin
total pipeline latency within product SLA with specialist architecture
revisit_triggers: frontier model capability improves making specialist gap shrink
task broadens reducing specialist advantage

nodes.definition: Design orchestration layer for routing requests to appropriate fine-tuned specialist adapters, managing adapter hot-swap, and controlling latency/cost compounding.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: adapter count changes; SLA requirements change; new serving framework adopted

pros.claim: Adapter hot-swapping enables serving multiple specializations from one base model reducing memory footprint
pros.example: S-LoRA: serving 1000 LoRA adapters on shared base with <10ms switching overhead

cons.claim: Orchestration adds latency and complexity; cascading specialist calls compound cost super-linearly
cons.example: 3-hop multi-specialist pipeline at 200ms each = 600ms vs 350ms direct GPT-4 call

failure_modes: adapter routing misclassification sending requests to wrong specialist
not profiling adapter swap latency under concurrent load
acceptance_tests: adapter routing accuracy >95% on held-out routing test set
p99 latency within product SLA under 2x peak load
revisit_triggers: adapter count grows beyond cache capacity
SLA requirements tighten

nodes.definition: Implement checkpoint saving strategy, early stopping criteria based on validation metric, and best-checkpoint selection to prevent over-training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training dynamics change; new early stopping methodology adopted

pros.claim: Early stopping on validation metric prevents epoch-level over-training and format memorization
pros.example: stopping at epoch 2 of 5 based on val loss prevents GSM8K accuracy collapse from over-training

cons.claim: Too-aggressive early stopping may stop before model converges on low-data regimes
cons.example: patience=1 epoch stops training prematurely when validation metric is noisy

failure_modes: checkpointing too infrequently losing training progress on preempted jobs
using training loss not validation metric for early stopping criterion
acceptance_tests: best checkpoint selected by validation metric not training epoch number
checkpoint recovery tested on simulated preemption
revisit_triggers: training infrastructure changes affecting checkpoint format
new training framework adopted

nodes.definition: Define and enforce quality standards for instruction-response pairs: format consistency, response length distribution, instruction diversity, and quality scoring rubric.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task definition changes; quality rubric expert review

pros.claim: High diversity and quality instructions produce more capable generalist SFT models than sheer quantity
pros.example: LIMA: 1000 high-quality diverse instructions outperform 50K noisy Alpaca-style data

cons.claim: Strict quality filters can eliminate edge-case coverage needed for robustness
cons.example: filtering short responses removes valid yes/no answers from classification tasks

failure_modes: instruction format inconsistency causing model to learn spurious format correlations
response quality rubric not aligned with task eval metric
acceptance_tests: format consistency >98% on random 500-example audit
instruction diversity metric (self-BLEU <0.4) confirmed on dataset
revisit_triggers: task definition changes requiring new instruction format
quality rubric updated by domain experts

nodes.definition: Apply gradient checkpointing, flash attention, and mixed precision to reduce peak activation memory and enable larger batch sizes or longer sequence training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: flash attention API changes; new GPU architecture; sequence length requirements change

pros.claim: Flash attention 2 + gradient checkpointing reduces memory 60-70% enabling 2-4x longer sequences
pros.example: 128K context Mistral training feasible on 8xA100 with flash attention 2 + activation offload

cons.claim: Gradient checkpointing recomputes activations on backward pass, adding 30-40% training time overhead
cons.example: training throughput drops from 2500 to 1700 tokens/sec/GPU with full gradient checkpointing

failure_modes: enabling gradient checkpointing without flash attention 2 causing OOM on long sequences
not profiling peak memory per step causing surprise OOM late in training
acceptance_tests: peak GPU memory utilization <90% confirmed on longest sequences in dataset
training throughput within 2x of theoretical peak for batch size
revisit_triggers: new flash attention version changes API
target sequence length increases

nodes.definition: Assess and mitigate safety risks introduced by SFT: harmful instruction following, jailbreak surface expansion, and misalignment from training data bias.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new jailbreak vector or red-team finding; deployment context changes

pros.claim: SFT on curated safe data reduces harmful outputs vs base model; refusal calibration prevents over-refusal
pros.example: SFT on safety-curated data reduces harmful output rate from 8% to 1.2% on red-team eval

cons.claim: SFT on task data without safety controls can expand jailbreak surface or erode base model refusals
cons.example: code SFT unintentionally teaches model to follow harmful code generation instructions

failure_modes: not red-teaming fine-tuned model assuming base model safety transfers
over-calibrating refusals reducing legitimate task utility
acceptance_tests: red-team harmful output rate below threshold on safety eval suite
refusal rate on legitimate task prompts within acceptable range
revisit_triggers: new jailbreak vector discovered; deployment context changes

edges.resolution_rule: benchmark quantized vs fp16 LoRA on validation metric; accept QLoRA if gap <2pp else upgrade GPU

edges.label: SFT task training conflicts with preservation of general capability
edges.resolution_rule: include 5-10% replay data from general instruction set; measure forgetting on benchmark suite

edges.label: multi-specialist orchestration latency/cost may exceed single generalist call
edges.resolution_rule: measure end-to-end pipeline latency and cost vs single frontier model call; use specialists only if clear win

edges.label: benchmark score optimization diverges from true capability due to Goodhart effect
edges.resolution_rule: maintain private eval set not used for training decisions; include human eval as Goodhart check

edges.label: restrictive base model license may block specialist deployment or redistribution
edges.resolution_rule: consult legal before committing to base model; establish approved use-case list before training

conflict_axes.name: task_performance_vs_general_capability
conflict_axes.tension: Maximizing task-specific SFT performance degrades general instruction-following and world knowledge
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: 5-10% general instruction replay; monitor MMLU/HellaSwag alongside task metric

conflict_axes.name: quantization_quality_vs_compute_cost
conflict_axes.tension: QLoRA 4-bit quantization reduces GPU cost 4-8x but introduces numerical noise degrading task performance
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: benchmark QLoRA vs fp16 LoRA on validation; accept QLoRA if gap <2pp else use fp16

conflict_axes.name: lora_rank_capacity_vs_memory_efficiency
conflict_axes.tension: Higher LoRA rank captures more task signal but increases VRAM and training time proportionally
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: start r=16; ablate up to r=64; return minimal rank achieving plateau

conflict_axes.name: data_quantity_vs_data_quality
conflict_axes.tension: More training data improves coverage but introduces noise that degrades instruction-following quality
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: quality-filter first; prefer LIMA-style 1K high-quality over 100K noisy; validate with held-out metric

conflict_axes.name: benchmark_score_vs_true_capability
conflict_axes.tension: Optimizing SFT for benchmark metrics triggers Goodhart's law, inflating scores without real capability gain
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: hold private eval set; include human eval; decontaminate training data from benchmarks

conflict_axes.name: specialist_depth_vs_orchestration_cost
conflict_axes.tension: Fine-tuned specialists outperform on narrow tasks but multi-step orchestration compounds latency and cost super-linearly
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: profile end-to-end pipeline vs single frontier model; prefer specialist only if clear performance+cost win

conflict_axes.name: model_license_openness_vs_deployment_rights
conflict_axes.tension: Open-weight models (LLaMA-style) offer fine-tunability but impose redistribution and commercial use constraints
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: classify license before training; prefer Apache-2.0 models for unrestricted deployment

conflict_axes.name: safety_refusal_calibration_vs_task_utility
conflict_axes.tension: Over-calibrating SFT model refusals reduces harmful outputs but also blocks legitimate task instructions
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: measure refusal rate on both harmful red-team set and legitimate task set; tune jointly

conflict_axes.name: adapter_modularity_vs_inference_latency
conflict_axes.tension: Keeping adapters separate enables multi-task hot-swapping but adds per-request latency vs merged model
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: profile swap latency under peak load; merge for latency-critical single-task; keep separate for multi-tenant

conflict_axes.name: training_epoch_count_vs_overfitting
conflict_axes.tension: More training epochs improve task convergence on small datasets but risk format memorization and benchmark overfit
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use validation loss early stopping with patience 1-2 epochs; monitor held-out task metric not train loss

edge_cases.description: Base model ToS prohibits fine-tuned derivative redistribution discovered after training completes
edge_cases.recommended_action: halt deployment; retrain on Apache-2.0 base; record ToS check in pre-training checklist

edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination detected: training data contains n-gram overlap with eval benchmark test set
edge_cases.trigger: MinHash dedup between train and eval
edge_cases.recommended_action: remove contaminated examples; re-run dedup; rerun evaluation; note all prior scores invalid

edge_cases.description: SFT causes catastrophic forgetting: MMLU drops 8pp while task F1 improves 20pp
edge_cases.recommended_action: add 5-10% general instruction replay; reduce learning rate; re-run training

edge_cases.description: QLoRA quantization degrades task performance >3pp vs fp16 LoRA baseline
edge_cases.recommended_action: switch to fp16 LoRA; upgrade GPU tier or apply gradient checkpointing to reduce memory

edge_cases.description: LoRA adapter merged into quantized base model produces precision mismatch artifacts corrupting outputs
edge_cases.recommended_action: dequantize base before merging; validate merged model output against unmerged adapter output

edge_cases.description: Chat template mismatch between training and inference causes runaway generation or wrong stop token
edge_cases.recommended_action: lock template version in model card; test generation terminates correctly before deployment

edge_cases.description: Multi-specialist pipeline latency exceeds SLA due to orchestration overhead compounding
edge_cases.recommended_action: profile each hop latency; collapse multi-hop pipeline or replace with single frontier model call

edge_cases.description: LoRA target modules list references layer names not present in selected model family
edge_cases.trigger: Model loading error at training start
edge_cases.recommended_action: programmatically verify target module names against model.named_modules() before training

edge_cases.description: SFT fine-tuned model exhibits jailbreak surface expansion: follows harmful instructions base model refused
edge_cases.recommended_action: add safety examples to SFT data; run DPO alignment on harmfulness refusals

edge_cases.description: Loss masking misconfiguration causes model to learn to predict prompt tokens, degrading instruction following
edge_cases.trigger: Anomalously low training loss early in epoch
edge_cases.recommended_action: inspect loss mask; verify prompt token positions masked to -100; compare with reference implementation

edge_cases.description: DoRA magnitude vectors become NaN or collapse to zero during training on low-rank configuration
edge_cases.recommended_action: switch to standard LoRA; check PEFT library version; file bug report

edge_cases.description: Gradient checkpointing enabled without flash attention 2 causes OOM on sequences >4K tokens
edge_cases.trigger: OOM error during training on long sequences
edge_cases.recommended_action: install flash-attn 2; enable attn_implementation='flash_attention_2' in model loading

workflow.action: Conduct go/no-go SFT analysis vs prompting baseline; define task spec
gates: specialist outperforms prompting on target metric

workflow.action: Select and license-audit base model; record ToS compliance
gates: legal sign-off on license for deployment use-case

workflow.action: Curate, deduplicate, and quality-filter training dataset; run benchmark contamination check
gates: no eval-set overlap; quality metrics pass

workflow.action: Apply chat template and configure tokenizer; verify loss masking
gates: loss mask confirmed on prompt tokens; EOS token present

workflow.action: Plan compute budget; select QLoRA or fp16 LoRA; configure memory optimizations
gates: peak memory within 90% GPU capacity on 100-step pilot

workflow.action: Configure LoRA adapter: select rank/alpha, target modules; optionally select DoRA
gates: target modules verified in model; parameter count within budget

workflow.action: Select hyperparameters; run pilot training for 100-200 steps; confirm smooth loss curve
gates: no loss spikes in pilot; gradient norms stable

workflow.action: Execute full SFT training loop with checkpoint management and early stopping
gates: validation loss lower than base; early stopping triggered before overfit

workflow.action: Evaluate fine-tuned model: task metrics, general benchmarks, contamination, human eval
gates: task metric improved; general benchmarks within 2pp of base; human eval agreement >0.7

workflow.action: Run safety red-teaming on fine-tuned model; calibrate refusals
gates: harmful output rate below threshold; refusal rate on legitimate prompts acceptable

workflow.action: Merge adapter into base model (or configure multi-adapter serving); deploy and profile latency
gates: merged model output matches unmerged within tolerance; latency within SLA

workflow.action: Monitor production: task metric drift, general capability regression, safety incidents
gates: metrics within control limits; safety incidents below threshold

dominance_rules.rule: LICENSE_TOS dominates BASE_MODEL_SEL: if license blocks deployment use-case, model must be replaced regardless of capability
DATA_CURATION dominates LORA_CONFIG: data quality improvements yield larger gains than rank tuning on low-data regimes
dominance_rules.condition: dataset quality is low or noisy
dominance_rules.rationale: garbage-in garbage-out; rank tuning cannot fix data quality

dominance_rules.rule: SAFETY_ALIGNMENT dominates ADAPTER_MERGE: safety red-team must pass before any deployment artifact is created
dominance_rules.rationale: jailbreak surface expansion is critical production risk

dominance_rules.rule: GOODHART_BENCH dominates EVAL_HARNESS: contamination audit must complete before benchmark scores are reported
dominance_rules.rationale: contaminated eval scores invalidate all downstream decisions

dominance_rules.rule: SPECIALIST_VS_GENERALIST dominates all PEFT nodes: if specialist does not beat prompting baseline, SFT is not justified
dominance_rules.rationale: avoids wasted compute on unnecessary fine-tuning

dominance_rules.rule: CAT_FORGETTING dominates SFT_LOOP configuration: anti-forgetting replay must be included if general benchmarks are critical
dominance_rules.condition: production system requires general instruction following
dominance_rules.rationale: silent capability degradation is worse than slightly reduced task peak

dominance_rules.rule: CHAT_TEMPLATE dominates DATA_FORMAT_QUALITY: correct template takes precedence over format quality standards when they conflict
dominance_rules.condition: template requires format incompatible with quality spec
dominance_rules.rationale: template error causes inference-time failure; format quality is secondary

dominance_rules.rule: COMPUTE_BUDGET dominates LORA_CONFIG: VRAM constraints dictate maximum feasible rank before quality optimization
dominance_rules.rationale: OOM aborts training; resource constraint is hard; rank is soft

dominance_rules.rule: CHECKPOINT_MGT dominates HYPERPARAM_TUNING: best checkpoint selection by validation metric overrides epoch-number heuristic
dominance_rules.rationale: loss-based early stopping is more reliable than fixed epoch count

dominance_rules.rule: BASE_MODEL_SEL dominates CHAT_TEMPLATE: model tokenizer determines valid template; template cannot override tokenizer
dominance_rules.rationale: tokenizer is immutable artifact of base model; template must conform to it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change base model after chat template and dataset tokenization are complete
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: full re-tokenization of entire dataset required

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not revise SFT training data after contamination deduplication completes and eval hashes are recorded
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: all benchmark scores invalidated; dedup must re-run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not alter LoRA target modules after QLoRA quantized training begins
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: training run invalidated; full restart from checkpoint

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not merge adapter into base model before safety red-team passes
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: deployed artifact must be recalled; repeat full safety eval cycle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not report benchmark scores before contamination audit completes
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: published scores must be retracted; reputational damage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize hyperparameters without pilot run confirming stable gradient norms
anti_rework_rules.trigger_for_rework: loss spike in full run traced to lr misconfiguration
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: full training run wasted; pilot is cheap insurance

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select rank without first confirming target module list and VRAM budget
anti_rework_rules.trigger_for_rework: OOM at training start due to rank too high for VRAM
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: training restart required; VRAM profiling must precede rank selection

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy fine-tuned model without validating chat template matches inference serving config
anti_rework_rules.trigger_for_rework: template mismatch causing generation failures in production

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not assume base model safety properties transfer to fine-tuned model without re-evaluation
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: emergency rollback; full safety cycle repeated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not commit to multi-adapter orchestration without profiling swap latency under concurrent load
anti_rework_rules.trigger_for_rework: SLA violation in production under peak load
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: architecture revision required; potential model merge forced post-deployment

iteration_protocol.trigger: Validation loss increases for 2 consecutive epochs
iteration_protocol.action: reduce learning rate by 0.5x; revert to last best checkpoint; increase gradient accumulation
add 5-10% general instruction replay data; re-run training from scratch with updated dataset mix

iteration_protocol.trigger: QLoRA task metric >2pp below fp16 LoRA baseline
iteration_protocol.action: switch to fp16 LoRA; apply gradient checkpointing + flash attention 2 to fit in VRAM

iteration_protocol.trigger: Benchmark contamination detected in training data
iteration_protocol.action: remove contaminated examples; re-run MinHash dedup; invalidate all prior benchmark scores; retrain if >1% of data affected

iteration_protocol.trigger: Safety red-team failure rate exceeds threshold
iteration_protocol.action: add safety-curated examples to SFT mix; consider DPO alignment layer; repeat red-team

iteration_protocol.trigger: Multi-specialist pipeline p99 latency exceeds SLA by >20%
iteration_protocol.action: profile each hop; collapse lowest-value hop; consider merging adapters or switching to larger single model

iteration_protocol.trigger: LoRA rank ablation shows <0.5pp gain from r=16 to r=32
iteration_protocol.action: lock rank at r=16; do not increase; investigate target module selection instead

iteration_protocol.trigger: OOM error during training on long sequences
iteration_protocol.action: enable flash attention 2; enable gradient checkpointing; reduce batch size; increase gradient accumulation steps

iteration_protocol.trigger: Task metric plateaus with more data but human eval shows quality regression
iteration_protocol.action: apply LIMA-style quality filtering; reduce dataset to highest-quality subset; re-evaluate

priority_rationale: License and base model selection first (legal/strategic gates); specialist/generalist go-no-go second (avoids wasted training); data pipeline next (data quality is highest-leverage lever); PEFT configuration before training; training loop and checkpointing; evaluation and safety before deployment artifacts; DoRA last (optional advanced PEFT variant); multi-adapter orchestration last (only needed for multi-specialist deployments)

expected_properties: task metric computable from fine-tuned model
LoRA adapter config validated before training

task metric improves but MMLU drops 5pp post-SFT
expected_properties: forgetting detected by general benchmark eval

expected_properties: deployment blocked until safety eval passes
